entry.title: 0.1.0-alpha.2
entry.content:
An alpha that fixes the update check. If you are on 0.1.0-alpha.1, install this one
over it — it is signed with the same key, so nothing has to be uninstalled and no data
is touched.

What was wrong

The check could report "could not connect to the update source" on a phone whose browser
opens the very same URL without trouble. Three different things were reported as that one
sentence, and a fourth — a reply that arrived but could not be parsed — was reported as a
network failure as well, a state the code could not even reach.

What changed

  • Every failure now says what it was: nothing reachable, no answer in time, a refusal
    that passes on its own (GitHub answers 403 or 429 when too many anonymous requests come
    from one address), a repository that is not there, any other status code named with its
    number, and a reply that could not be read. Each has its own sentence in all nine
    languages.
  • The check no longer depends on one endpoint. When the API refuses the request or
    answers with something unreadable, the app now reads the repository release feed at
    github.com/stephen2754/budge/releases.atom — served by the same host as this release
    page, and not subject to the API quota of sixty anonymous requests an hour per address.
  • The request waits 20 seconds instead of 10, which a slow international route can
    need before it wrongly reports the device as offline.

None of these states ever says the build is up to date.

Install

  • Package: com.example.budge
  • Version: 0.1.0-alpha.2 (versionCode 2)
  • Size: 1614909 bytes
  • SHA-256: ddc4da35371fef1411769490e9ac60069a078477ef24406f2c2ebe22881471bf
  • Signing certificate SHA-256: b13ab2ef2bac6617572b7822f4d4ae09ebe5184358dd45a1f89096c69132eeb0

If the check still fails

It will now say which of the six things happened. Send me that sentence — it names the
cause, and with the old build there was no way to tell.

entry.title: 0.1.0-alpha.1
entry.content:
The first published build of Budge, an alpha. The app is usable and the ledger
features below are complete, but expect rough edges — this is an unstable test build, so
major problems are possible.

Install

Download budge-0.1.0-alpha.1.apk below and open it on a device running Android 8.0 or
newer. You will have to allow installing from this source, since the build is signed
with a key you have never seen before. That key is stable from now on, so later releases
install over this one without uninstalling it.

  • Package: com.example.budge
  • Version: 0.1.0-alpha.1 (versionCode 1)
  • Size: 1,592,229 bytes
  • SHA-256: 40494483fb5efac4080c8dead56d58dd3c282b2bab25d0e85e139668a2554c2d
  • Signing certificate SHA-256: b13ab2ef2bac6617572b7822f4d4ae09ebe5184358dd45a1f89096c69132eeb0

What is in it

  • Record an expense or income in a few taps: type, amount, category, note, date, time.
  • Home shows the month as a day-grouped list with daily subtotals, a monthly summary
    and swipe-to-delete.
  • Statistics by year, month or day: totals, balance, and a per-category breakdown as a
    donut chart. One date anchors all three periods.
  • Categories are seeded on first launch in the device language and are ordinary rows
    afterwards: rename, re-colour, re-type or delete any of them.
  • Nine languages — English, 中文, Français, Deutsch, Español, Русский, 日本語, Italiano,
    Português — plus a choice of currency sign, which groups the common currencies that
    share one.
  • Backup to a JSON file you choose and restore from one, with the file validated
    before anything is overwritten.
  • Settings for currency, theme, language, categories and data, with an About section
    holding the release history, third-party licences and the update check.

No account, no sync, no analytics. Records live in a local Room database and preferences
in DataStore. The update check is the only network request the app can make, and it is a
read-only GET for this release list that carries no ledger data.

Known limitations

  • No screen sets a monthly budget yet, although the table, DAO and the statistics card for
    one exist.
  • Category icons are stored but never drawn; lists show the category's initial.
  • Unit tests cover formatting, storage ranges, backup and the update rules; there are no
    instrumentation or UI tests.
  • Lint cannot run on a machine whose Android SDK ships platform-tools 37.x — the pinned
    AGP 8.7.3 cannot parse that version string, so release builds skip the vital check.

Updating

This build is an alpha, so its update check is offered everything: alpha, beta and stable
releases. Later versions appear under Settings → About → Check for updates, and a check
that cannot reach GitHub reports that it could not tell, never "up to date".
